rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Anadromous fish leave the sea to breed in fresh water. Hilsa does this in Terai rivers.
Catadromous fish leave fresh water to breed in the sea. The eel Anguilla is the example.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Migration is two-way and seasonal; one-way dispersal or permanent emigration is NOT migration.  ·  Anadromous = sea → river to breed; catadromous = river → sea to breed — do not swap the arrows.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Keep the course example attached to the right class.  ·  A direction word (to sea, to fresh water, in-situ, ex-situ) is part of the mark.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Hilsa ascending Terai rivers in monsoon to spawn (anadromous).  ·  Siberian ducks wintering at Koshi Tappu, returning north in spring (latitudinal bird migration).

rows.text: **Short answer (2):** Define migration and distinguish it from dispersal and emigration. **Answer.** **Migration** — a periodic, **two-way** (return) movement of a population between breeding and non-breeding grounds, usually seasonal.…  ·  **Short answer (3):** Differentiate anadromous and catadromous fish migration with one example of each. **Answer.** | Basis | Anadromous | Catadromous | |---|---|---| | Adult life | Sea | Freshwater river | | Spawning migration | **Up rivers** to spawn | **Down to the sea** to spawn | | Example | Salmon, Hilsa | Eel |

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: [Remember] Migration is the periodic, seasonal, two-way movement of animals between breeding and non-breeding habitats — distinct from one-way dispersal or permanent emigration.  ·  [Remember] Fish migration: anadromous fishes move from sea to fresh water to breed (e.g. Hilsa ilisha ascending Terai rivers in monsoon); catadromous fishes move from fresh water to sea to breed (e.g. eels, Anguilla).  ·  [Understand] Bird migration types: latitudinal or north–south (Siberian ducks wintering at Koshi Tappu and Chitwan), longitudinal, and altitudinal (pheasants and thrushes descending from hills to Terai in winter).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Altitudinal migration (hills ↔ Terai) is still migration even though the distance is short.  ·  Homing instinct and banding studies prove return journeys; do not claim birds 'get lost and stay'.  ·  Latitudinal bird migration brings Siberian ducks to Koshi Tappu and Chitwan in winter.
